Stationary points are where the derivative of a function equals zero. So, first, take the derivative of f(x) (f'(x)). Then set it equal to zero and solve for x. Those x-values are the critical points. To check if they’re maxima or minima, you’d look at the second derivative (f''(x))—if it’s positive, it’s a minimum; if negative, a maximum. You start by standardizing the data, then compute the covariance matrix and find its eigenvalues/eigenvectors. The eigenvectors with the largest eigenvalues become your principal components.
